findings.title: Partition lock creation is racy
findings.body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads and writes self.partition_locks dict without any synchronization. Two threads calling add_offset/complete_offset for a new Partition can both miss in .get() and setdefault different Lock objects, so callers end up holding different locks and all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed are mutated without mutual exclusion. This corrupts committable-offset computation leading to duplicate processing or skipped commits.

findings.title: Committable scan loops over full offset range
findings.body: get_committable_offsets does for offset in range(start, max_offset+1) over Kafka offsets. A single missing offset (gap from filtered/decode-failed or not-yet-seen message) leaves all later offsets in all_offsets forever, so the range grows unboundedly and this runs every second per partition. With large or sparse offsets this is CPU-heavy and all_offsets/outstanding grow without bound (memory leak) blocking all later commits.

findings.title: close() stops commits before draining workers
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread, then shuts down the queue pool. Any work item that completes after the commit thread exits will call complete_offset but never be turned into a commit via mark_committed/commit_function. On graceful shutdown processed messages are therefore never committed and will be reprocessed on restart, and there is no final flush.

findings.title: Offsets committed from background thread
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop runs in its own Thread and calls the Arroyo commit callable asynchronously every second, while submit/poll run on the StreamProcessor thread. Arroyo expects commit to be called from the processing thread for the owned partitions; concurrent commit during rebalance/shutdown can commit offsets for revoked partitions, race with StreamProcessor shutdown, and mark_committed races across multiple strategy instances sharing the same OffsetTracker.

findings.title: Single shared queue pool across partitions/rebalances
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool/OffsetTracker in __init__ and reuses it for every create_with_partitions call. Each call then creates a SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy with its own commit thread but sharing the tracker. Each commit thread calls its own partition-scoped commit with committable offsets for all partitions, misrouting commits, and close/terminate of one strategy shuts down the pool still used by other partitions.

findings.title: shutdown clears queue_pool breaking rebalance
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown shuts down the pool and sets self.queue_pool to None. Arroyo factories are long-lived and create_with_partitions is called again after a rebalance; create_thread_queue_parallel_worker then asserts queue_pool is not None and fails. The factory cannot serve new assignments after any shutdown/close.

findings.title: Failed work items marked complete and committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Despite the class docstring claiming only successful processing is committed, poison messages are treated as done and their offsets become committable, silently skipping data instead of blocking/retrying/DLQing.
